**Physical** — heat and cold cracking rocks; **chemical** — water and chemicals dissolving rocks; **biological** — plant roots and burrowing animals breaking rocks.

**Sandy** — large particles, drains very fast, poor at holding water; **clay** — very small particles, sticky when wet and hard when dry, holds too much water; **loam** — a mixture with plenty of humus, holds enough water and drains well.
**Loam**, because it holds enough water but still drains well, contains **air and plenty of humus**, and is easy to work.
**Clay**, because its very fine particles stick together when wet and become hard when dried or fired.

blocks.x: Vaccines are **spoilt by heat and by strong light**, so they must be kept cold from the factory to the child. This is called the **cold chain**.

blocks.x: **Primary Health Care (PHC):** Essential health care that is made available to all people in the community, at a cost they can afford, with their full participation.

Its aim is to **prevent disease** and promote health, rather than only to treat people after they fall sick. It is carried out **where people live** — in homes, villages and schools — and not only in hospitals.

Because preventing a disease **costs far less** than treating it, saves lives and suffering, keeps children in school and adults at work, and stops the disease from spreading to others.

**Community:** protect water sources; hold clean-up days; support village health teams; build and maintain health centres (also report outbreaks). **Government:** train and pay health workers; supply drugs and vaccines; build health centres; make and enforce public health laws (also run health campaigns).
A family is a group of people related by blood, marriage or adoption who live together and care for one another. Types: **nuclear, extended, single-parent and child-headed**.

**Parents:** provide food, shelter, clothing, medical care and education; give love, guidance and discipline; protect the children. **Children:** obey and respect parents; help with chores; go to school and work hard; care for younger ones and the elderly; keep clean; report anything that frightens or hurts them.

Give **clean bedding and a quiet, airy room**; provide soft, tasty food and plenty of fluids; give the **medicine on time and complete the dose**; keep the person clean and comfortable; watch for danger signs and **take them to a health worker quickly**.

**The elderly** need soft food, warmth, company, help with washing and moving, and **respect**. **People with disabilities** need support without pity, help to attend school and work, assistive aids where possible, and full **inclusion** in family activities.
Any six of: a clean compound; a latrine; a rubbish pit; a drying rack; a bath shelter; a kitchen with a raised fireplace; clean covered water storage; mosquito nets on the beds; a kitchen garden.

Village health teams are **trained community volunteers**. They teach families about health, encourage immunisation and use of latrines and nets, treat or refer simple illnesses, follow up sick people and report outbreaks.

Any four of: keeping the compound and latrines clean; running hand-washing points with soap; a school health club with drama, posters and talks; growing vegetables in a school garden; inspecting pupils' hygiene; inviting health workers; deworming and immunisation days.
